lines.vo: Why can daydreaming about your goal make it harder to reach?
That's not bad luck. Your brain feels like it already arrived.
So Tasha writes her goal and the obstacle in her Life Reset Planner.
In experiments at New York University, people who only pictured a perfect outcome showed less energy.
It's as if the brain gets a taste of the win before doing any of the work.
What tends to work better is mental contrasting. Picture the goal, then the obstacle in the way.
Then make a plan. If the obstacle shows up, then I'll do this.
Dream it, spot the snag, plan around it. That's how you stay on track.
